rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrected stand exposed, with no mountain, hill, or building screening them.
rows.anchor: ظاهرون لا يسترهم شىء من جبل أو اكمة أو بناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing about their deeds or circumstances is hidden from God.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء ﴾ اى من اعمالهم واحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks who owns sovereignty that day, then answers Himself; the sole sovereign has subdued creation through death.
rows.anchor: اى يقول الله تعالى ذلك حين لا أحد يجيبه ثم يجيب نفسه بقوله ﴿ لله الواحد القهار ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative has a caller ask who owns sovereignty, with the people gathered answering that it belongs to God, the One, the Subduer.
rows.anchor: وقيل ينادى مناد فيقول لمن الملك اليوم فيجيبه اهل المحشر لله الواحد القهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say God is their Lord profess monotheism and remain firm in that confession and its requirements.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ﴾ اى نطقوا بالتوحيد ﴿ ثم استقاموا ﴾ ثم ثبتوا على الاقرار ومقتضياته

rows.speaker: الصديق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr says they remained steadfast in deeds as they had in words; he also rejects the claim that steadfastness means never sinning, defining it as never returning to idol worship.
rows.anchor: وعن الصديق رضى الله عنه استقاموا فعلا كما استقاموا قولا وعنه انه تلاها ثم قال ما تقولون فيها قالوا لم يذنبوا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar explains steadfastness as not swerving like foxes, meaning not being hypocritical.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضى الله عنه لم يروغوا روغان الثعالب اى لم ينافقوا

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman says steadfast believers purify their deeds.
rows.anchor: وعن عثمان رضى الله عنه اخلصوا العمل

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says steadfastness means fulfilling the obligatory duties.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضى الله عنه ادوا الفرائض

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl describes steadfastness as renouncing the passing world and desiring the everlasting one.
rows.anchor: وعن الفضيل زهدوا في الفانية ورغبوا في الباقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition makes steadfastness continued adherence after professing faith, rather than fleeing after professing it.
rows.anchor: وقيل حقيقة الاستقامة القرار بعد الاقرار لا الفرار بعد الاقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend at death and tell believers not to fear what lies ahead or grieve over what they left behind.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عليهم الملائكة ﴾ عند الموت ان بمعنى اى أو مخففة من الثقيلة واصله بانه ﴿ ألا تخافوا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is grief in expectation of harm, whereas grief follows loss of benefit or the arrival of harm; God has secured them from every grief.
rows.anchor: فالخوف غم يلحق الانسان لتوقع المكروه والحزن غم يلحق لوقوعه من فوات نافع أو حصول ضار والمعنى ان الله كتب لكم الامن من كل غم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised Paradise is the one believers were promised in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأبشروا بالجنة التي كنتم توعدون ﴾ في الدنيا

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذى
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi says the angels of the Merciful descend as souls leave bodies, reassuring believers against loss of faith and past disobedience and announcing Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي الترمذى تتنزل عليهم ملائكة الرحمن عند مفارقة الارواح الابدان ان لا تخافوا سلب الايمان ولا تحزنوا على ما كان من العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jawari is the plural of jariya and denotes ships.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن آياته الجوار ﴾ جمع جارية وهى السفينة

rows.speaker: مكى وسهل ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers retain the yāʾ in al-jawari in both grammatical states; the Medinan reader and Abu Amr agree in connected recitation.
rows.anchor: الجوارى في الحالين مكى وسهل ويعقوب وافقهم مدنى وابو عمر وفي الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships at sea are like mountains in size and appearance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ في البحر كالأعلام ﴾ كالجبال

rows.speaker: مدنى
rows.claim: The Medinan reading has al-riyah, winds, in place of al-rih, wind.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن يشأ يسكن الريح ﴾ الرياح مدنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God stills the wind, ships remain motionless on the sea's surface.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فيظللن رواكد ﴾ ثوابت لا تجرى ﴿ على ظهره ﴾ على ظهر البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are for everyone who patiently bears affliction and gives thanks for blessings, that is, the sincere believer.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار ﴾ على بلائه ﴿ شكور ﴾ لنعمائه اى لكل مؤمن مخلص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers two formulations: faith has two halves, gratitude and patience; or the believer is patient in obedience and grateful for God's blessing.
rows.anchor: فالايمان نصفان نصف شكر ونصف صبر أو صبار على طاعته شكور لنعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commanded to adhere to the Quran and act by it, since he follows a straight, unbending religion.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاستمسك ﴾ فتمسك ﴿ بالذي أوحي إليك ﴾ وهو القرآن واعمل به ﴿ إنك على صراط مستقيم ﴾ اى على الدين الذى لا عوج له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh either personally summoned Egypt's nobles or ordered a herald to do so, as one may say the emir cut a thief when he ordered it.
rows.anchor: نادى بنفسه عظماء القبط أو أمر مناديا فنادى كقولك قطع الأمير اللص اذا أمر بقطعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in his people makes them the place and audience of his call.
rows.anchor: ﴿ في قومه ﴾ جعلهم محلا لندائه وموقعا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers are the Nile's waterways, most notably four.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال يا قوم أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار ﴾ أي أنهار النيل ومعظمها أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under me may mean beneath Pharaoh's palace, or in front of him in his gardens.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تجري من تحتي ﴾ من تحت قصرى وقيل بين يدى في جنائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis coordinates the rivers with Egypt's kingdom and makes their flowing a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: والواو عاطفة للانهار على ملك مصر وتجرى نصب على الحال منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the waw is circumstantial, this is a subject, the rivers describe it, and their flowing is its predicate.
rows.anchor: أو الواو للحال واسم الاشارة مبتدأ والانهار صفة لاسم الاشارة وتجرى خبر للمبتدأ

rows.speaker: الرشيد
rows.claim: After reading the verse, al-Rashid vowed to assign Egypt to his lowliest servant and gave it to al-Khasib, formerly his ablution attendant.
rows.anchor: وعن الرشيد انه لما قرأها قال لاولينها اخس عبيدى فولاها الخصيب وكان خادمة على وضوئه

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Tahir judged Egypt less worthy than Pharaoh's boast implied, then turned his horse away rather than enter it.
rows.anchor: وعن عبدالله بن طاهر أنه وليها فخرج اليها فلما شارفها قال أهى القرية التي افتخر بها فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's challenge mocks Moses by contrasting his own youth and strength and wealth with Moses' weakness and poverty.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أفلا تبصرون ﴾ فوتى وضعف موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community is seen kneeling, sitting on its knees; another gloss takes the word to mean gathered together.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وترى كل أمة جاثية ﴾ جالسة على الركب يقال جثا فلان يجثو اذا جلس عل ركبتيه وقيل جاثية مجتمعة

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads kullu in the nominative as a new subject, while his accusative reading is an appositive to umma.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كل أمة ﴾ بالرفع على الابتداء كل بالفتح يعقوب عل الابدال من كل أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community is summoned to its record, meaning the pages of its deeds; the generic singular book suffices.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تدعى إلى كتابها ﴾ إلى صحائف اعمالها فاكتفى باسم الجنس فيقال لهم ﴿ اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون ﴾ في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day people are recompensed for what they did in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ﴿ اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون ﴾ في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record is attributed to people because their deeds are recorded in it, and to God because He owns it and ordered the angels to write His servants' deeds.
rows.anchor: اضيف الكتاب اليهم لملابسته اياهم لان اعمالهم مثبتة فيه والى الله تعالى لانه مالكه والآمر ملائكته ان يكتبوا فيه اعمال عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book speaks by bearing witness against people about what they did.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ينطق ﴾ ﴿ عليكم بالحق إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون ﴾ ﴿ عليكم ﴾ يشهد عليكم بما عملتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its testimony is true, with neither addition nor omission.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بالحق ﴾ من غير زيادة ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istinsakh may mean having the angels write down deeds; alternatively, it is synonymous with naskh and means establishing them, not copying them from another book.
rows.anchor: اى نستكتب الملائكة اعمالكم وقيل نسخت واستنسخت بمعنى وليس ذلك بنقل من كتاب بل معناه نثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the heavens, earth, and all worlds; this universal lordship obliges every creature under His care to praise and extol Him.
rows.anchor: فاحمدوا الله الذى هو ربكم ورب كل شىء من السموات والأرض والعالمين فإن مثل هذه الربوبية العامة توجب الحمد والثناء على كل مربوب

rows.speaker: كوفى
rows.claim: The Kufan reading takes ihsanan as an accusative verbal object: God enjoined people to treat parents well with good treatment.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه إحسانا ﴾ كوفى اى وصيناه بأن يحسن بوالديه احسانا حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings take the phrase as a good command concerning one's parents, or as a command of goodness, in apposition to parents by inclusion.
rows.anchor: غيرهم اى وصيناه بوالديه امرا ذا حسن أو بأمر ذى حسن فهو في موضع البدل من قوله بوالديه وهو من بدل الاشتمال

rows.speaker: حجازى وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Hijazi and Abu Amr readings open the kāf in karhan; both vowelings are Arabic forms meaning hardship.
rows.anchor: وبفتح الكافين حجازى وأبو عمرو وهما لغتان في معنى المشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karhan may be parsed circumstantially, meaning in hardship, or as an adjective of the verbal noun, a burdensome carrying or delivery.
rows.anchor: وانتصابه على الحال اى ذات كره أو على انه صفة للمصدر اى حملا ذاكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Carrying and fisal refer to the period of pregnancy and weaning.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وحمله وفصاله ﴾ ومدة حمله و فطامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thirty-month total proves that pregnancy can last as little as six months, after subtracting the two full nursing years stated in 2:233.
rows.anchor: اقل مدة الحمل ستة اشهر لان مدة الرضاع ا ذا كانت حولين لقوله تعالى حولين كاملين بقيت للحمل ستة أشهر

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad infer a six-month minimum pregnancy from the thirty-month total and two years of nursing.
rows.anchor: وبه قال أبو يوسف ومحمد رحمهما الله

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa gives a different interpretation, glossing the span with the phrase al-haml bil-akaff.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضى الله عنه المراد به الحمل بالأكف

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads fisalah as faslah; the two verbal nouns are alike in form and meaning, as ʿazm and ʿizam are.
rows.anchor: وفصله يعقوب والفصل والفصال كالعظم والعظام بناء ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd has no singular from the same word form; reaching maturity means becoming fully adult and attaining one's strength and reason, around after thirty and approaching forty.
rows.anchor: هو جمع لا واحد له من لفظه وكان سيبويه يقول واحدة شدة وبلوغ الاشد ان يكتهل ويستوفى السن التى فيها قوته وعقله وذلك اذا أناف على الثلاثين وناطح الاربعين

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh gives shiddah as the singular of ashudd.
rows.anchor: وكان سيبويه يقول واحدة شدة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah sets the age at thirty-three as the beginning of full maturity and forty as its limit.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة ثلاث وثلاثون سنة ووجهه ان يكون ذلك اول الأشد وغايته الأربعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awziʿni means inspire or enable me; the blessing on the parents is included because their blessing is also a blessing on the child.
rows.anchor: قال رب أوزعني ﴾ الهمنى ﴿ أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي ﴾ المراد به نعمة التوحيد والاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed gloss identifies the righteous work requested as the five prayers.
rows.anchor: قيل هى الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for reform in one's descendants asks that they become a locus and likely occasion of righteousness; repentance is from every sin, and being Muslim here means sincerity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأصلح لي في ذريتي ﴾ اى اجعل ذريتى موقعا للصلاح ومظنة له ﴿ إني تبت إليك ﴾ من كل ذنب ﴿ وإني من المسلمين ﴾ من المخلصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from the Messenger's religion and Sunnah risks a return to pre-Islamic corruption: raiding, plunder, fighting relatives, and burying daughters.
rows.anchor: ان اعرضتم عن دين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسنته ان ترجعوا إلى ما كنتم عليه في الجاهلية من الافساد في الأرض بالتغاور والتناهب وقطع الارحام بمقاتلة بعض الاقارب بعضا ووأد البنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause interrupts between the subject of ʿasa and its predicate; the implied sense is whether you may corrupt and sever kinship if you turn away.
rows.anchor: وخبر عسى ان تفسدوا والشرط اعتراض بين الاسم والخبر والتقدير فهل عسيتم ان تفسدوا في الأرض تقطعوا ارحامكم ان توليتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatḥ is victory over a town by force or peace, in war or without it: what is closed becomes opened when conquered.
rows.anchor: الفتح الظفر بالبلدة عنوة أو صلحا بحرب أو بغير حرب لانه مغلق مالم يظفر به فاذا ظفر به فقد فتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the conquest as Mecca; the surah came on the Prophet's return from it in the year of Hudaybiyya as a promise of that victory.
rows.anchor: قيل هو فتح مكة وقد نزلت مرجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن مكة عام الحديبية عدة له بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense presents the promised conquest as already realized, giving the report grandeur and underscoring its importance.
rows.anchor: وجىء به لفظ على الماضى لانها فى تحققها بمنزلة الكائنة وفي ذلك من الفخامة والدلالة على علو شان المخبر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies it as Hudaybiyya: there was no major battle, but arrows and stones were exchanged until the Muslims drove the polytheists home and they sought peace.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو فتح الحديبية ولم يكن فيه قتال شديد ولكن ترام بين القوم بسهام وحجارة فرمى المسلمون المشركين حتى ادخلوهم ديارهم وسألوا الصلح

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls Hudaybiyya a great sign: after its water was depleted, the Prophet rinsed his mouth and spat into the well, which then flowed until all drank.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج كان في فتح الحديبية آية للمسلمين عظيمة وذلك انه نزح ماؤها ولم يبق فيها قطرة فتمضمض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم مجه في البئر فدرت بالماء حتى شرب جميع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another opinion identifies the conquest as Khaybar.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو فتح خيبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative understands the verse as God's clear decree that the Prophet and his companions would enter Mecca the following year and circumambulate the House.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه قضينا لك قضاء بينا على اهل مكة ان يدخلها انت واصحابك من قابلى لتطوفوا بالبيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this final reading, fatḥ comes from fatāḥa, adjudication or judgment.
rows.anchor: من الفتاحة وهى الحكومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading denies that conquest caused forgiveness and supplies an implied command to seek forgiveness, as in the closing of Surat al-Nasr.
rows.anchor: قيل الفتح ليس بسبب المغفرة والتقدير انا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا فاستغفر لك الله ومثله اذا جاء نصر الله والفتح إلى قوله فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, conquering Mecca through jihad against the enemy is itself a cause of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون فتح مكة من حيث انه جهاد للعدو سببا للغفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the conquest was for completing favor, guidance, and mighty victory, not for forgiveness; the blessings are joined because these are the greatest gifts and unite the honors of both abodes.
rows.anchor: وقيل الفتح لم يكن ليغفر له بل لاتمام النعمة وهداية الصراط المستقيم والنصر العزيز ولكنه لما عدد عليه هذه النعم وصلها بما هو اعظم النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss takes past and future sin to mean everything that proceeded from the Prophet or would proceed from him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ﴾ يريد جميع ما فرط منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A specific gloss takes the past matter as the episode of Mariya and the future matter as the affair of Zayd's wife.
rows.anchor: أو ما تقدم من حديث مارية وما تأخر من امرأة زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completes His favor by raising His religion and opening lands at the Prophet's hand.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويتم نعمته عليك ﴾ باعلاء دينك وفتح البلاد على يدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance to a straight path means keeping the Prophet firm on the approved religion.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويهديك صراطا مستقيما ﴾ يثبتك على الدين المرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The الدين here is recompense for deeds, and it will certainly come to pass.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإن الدين ﴾ الجزاء على الاعمال ﴿ لواقع ﴾ لكائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the idols worshipped apart from God possess the power and greatness attributed to the Lord of might.
rows.anchor: اى اخبرونا عن هذه الاشياء التى تعبدونها من دون اللهعز وجل هل لها من القدرة والعظمة التى وصف بها رب العزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat are female idols; al-Lat belonged to Thaqif at Taif, though another report places her at Nakhlah among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: اللات والعزى ومناة اصنام لهم وهى مؤنثات فاللات كان لثقيف بالطائف وقيل كانت بنهخلة تعبدها قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Lat's name is linked to those who frequented and remained there in worship.
rows.anchor: وهى فعلة من لوى لانهم كانوا يلوون عليها ويعكفون للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Uzza belonged to Ghatafan and was a samura tree; her name feminizes al-aʿazz, and Khalid ibn al-Walid cut it down.
rows.anchor: العزى كانت لغطفان وهى سمرة واصلها تأنيث الاعز وقطعها خالدين الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manat was a rock of Hudhayl and Khuzaa, or of Thaqif; its name is tied to sacrificial blood being shed there.
rows.anchor: ومناة صخرة كانت لهذيل وخزاعة وقيل لثقيف وكانها سميت مناة لان دماء النسائك كانت تمنى عندها اى تراق

rows.speaker: مكى
rows.claim: The Meccan reading is Minaʾa, derived from nawʾ; people sought rain at the idol in reverence for the star mansions.
rows.anchor: ومناءة مكى مفعلة من النوء كانهم كانوا يستمطرون عندها الانواء تبركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ukhra may be a disparaging description meaning late and low in rank, like the description of the last group in 7:38.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الأخرى ﴾ هى صفة ذم اى المتأخرة الوضيعة المقدار كقوله وقالت اخراهم لاولاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the idols were called last because the Arabs ranked al-Lat and al-Uzza ahead of them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان تكون الاولية والتقدم عندهم للات والعزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The irony is that they claimed angels and idols were God's daughters and their intercessors while burying daughters and despising them.
rows.anchor: كانوا يقولون ان الملائكة وهذه الاصنام بنات الله وكانوا يعبدونهم ويزعمون انهم شفعاؤهم عندالله مع وأدهم البنات وكراهتم لهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are names without real referents, since the names have been applied to things least deserving and most unlike divinity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن هي ﴾ ما الاصنام ﴿ إلا أسماء ﴾ ليس تحتها في الحقيقة مسميات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To name them means to call them by those names.
rows.anchor: ﴿ سميتموها ﴾ اى سميتم بها يقال سميته زيد أو سميته يزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has sent no proof authorizing their claims.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان ﴾ حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worship follows conjecture and what their souls desire.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن يتبعون إلا الظن ﴾ الا توهم ان ماهم عليه حق ﴿ وما تهوى الأنفس ﴾ وما تشتهيه انفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger and Scripture brought guidance from their Lord, but the idolaters abandoned it and did not act on it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى ﴾ الرسول والكتاب فتركوه ولم يعملوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-insan in the creation verse may mean humanity as a kind, Adam, or Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الرحمن علم القرآن خلق الإنسان ﴾ اى الجنس أو آدم أو محمدا عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descriptive phrase dhul-jalal is read in the Syrian tradition as an adjective of the name.
rows.anchor: لعظمة ذو الجال شامى صفة للاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's majesty and generosity are bestowed on His faithful servants through His beneficence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والإكرام ﴾ لاوليائه بالانعام

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet recited Surat al-Rahman and chided silent listeners, saying the jinn had responded better.
rows.anchor: روى جابر ان النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir's report says that whenever the Prophet recited the refrain, the jinn answered that they denied none of God's favors and praised and thanked Him.
rows.anchor: ما ايمت على قول الله فبأى آلاء ربكما تكذبان الا قالوا ولا بشىء من نعمك ربنا نكذب فلك الحمد ولك الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain occurs thirty-one times: eight follow signs of creation and the beginning and end of creation, seven follow descriptions of Hell and its terrors, then eight describe each of two pairs of gardens.
rows.anchor: وكررت هذه الاية في هذه السورة احدى وثلاثين مرة ذكر ثمانية منها عقب آيات فيها تعداد عجائب خلق الله وبدائع صنعه ومبدا الخلق ومعادهم ثم سبعة منها عقب آيات فيها ذكر انار وشدائدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight initial refrains are tied to the gates of Paradise and Hell: one who believes them and acts accordingly has Paradise's gates opened and Hell's closed.
rows.anchor: فمن اعتقد الثمانية الاولى وعمل بموجبها فتحت له ابواب الجنة واغلقت عنه ابواب جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to declare God free of what does not befit Him, or to glorify Him by remembering His name.
rows.anchor: فنزه ربكعما لا يليق به أيها المستمع المستدل أو أراد بالاسم الذكر أي سبح بذكر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿazim may describe the genitive annexed noun, or the noun to which it is annexed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ العظيم ﴾ صفة للمضاف أو للمضافاليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss takes the command to be the formula Subhana rabbi al-ʿazim.
rows.anchor: وقيل قل سبحان ربي العظيم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet instructed the believers to say it in bowing.
rows.anchor: وجاء مرفوعا أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال أجعلوها في ركوعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the soul, meaning the spirit, reaches the throat at death, it passes through the channel for food and drink.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلولا إذا بلغت ﴾ النفس أي الروح عند الموت ﴿ الحلقوم ﴾ ممر الطعام والشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is closer to the dying person, while the onlookers cannot see or understand His nearness.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ونحن أقرب إليه ﴾ إلى المحتضر ﴿ منكم ولكن لا تبصرون ﴾ لا تعقلون ولا تعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being غير مدينين means not being ruled or subject, from the verb for a ruler's governing his subjects.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلولا إن كنتم غير مدينين ﴾ مربوبين من دان السلطان الرعية اذاساسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is to return the soul or spirit to the body after it reaches the throat, if the deniers are truthful in claiming not to be ruled and subdued.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ترجعونها ﴾ تردون النفس وهي الروح إلى الجسد بعد بلوغ الحلقوم ﴿ إن كنتم صادقين ﴾ انكم غير مربوبين مقهورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences of laولا are exhortative and call for an action, namely returning the soul; the second mention is repeated for emphasis, with the intended order made explicit.
rows.anchor: فلولا في الآيتين للتحضيض يستدعى فعلا وذا قوله ترجعونها واكتفى بذكره مرة وترتيب الآية فلولا في ترجعونها اذا بلغت الحلقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is closer to the dying person by His power and knowledge, or through the angels of death.
rows.anchor: ونحن أقرب اليه منكم يا أهل الميت بقدرتنا وعلمنا أو بملائكة المت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge answers denial of God's signs: disbelievers call a miraculous Book magic or fabrication, a truthful messenger a sorcerer and liar, and rain a product of a star mansion.
rows.anchor: ان نزل عليكم كتابا معجزا قلتم سحر وافتراء ون ارسل اليكم رسولا صادقا قلتم ساحر كذاب وان رزقكم مطرا عليكم به قلتم نوء كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a doctrine leads to neglect and denial of divine action; if no one takes the soul and they are right, why cannot they restore it to the body?
rows.anchor: على مذهب يؤدي إلى الاهمال والتعطيل فما لكم لا ترجعون الروح إلى البدن بعد بلوغه الحلقوم إن لم يكن ثمة قابض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge targets their denial of the God who causes death, originates creation, and brings it back.
rows.anchor: وكنتم صادقين في تعطيلكم وكفركم بالمى المميت المبدئ المعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayb and al-shahada may mean the secret and manifest.
rows.anchor: ﴿ هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب والشهادة ﴾ أي السر والعلانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they mean this world and the next, or what is nonexistent and what exists.
rows.anchor: أو الدنيا والآخرة أو المعدوم والموجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Merciful and the Compassionate.
rows.anchor: هو الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the people under God's anger as polytheists, who despair of afterlife reward because they deny resurrection; the ظاهر replaces a pronoun.
rows.anchor: قيل هم المشركون ﴿ قد يئسوا من الآخرة ﴾ من ثوابها لأنهم ينكرون البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation compares them to their buried predecessors, who had despaired of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أو كما يئس أسلافهم الذين هم في القبور من الآخرة أي هؤلاء كسلفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as Jews, who despair of an afterlife share because they defy the Messenger despite recognizing him in the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم اليهود آي لا تتولوا قوما مغضوبا عليهم قد يئسوا من أن يكون لهم حظ في الآخرة لعنادهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم يعلمون أنه الرسول في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, the comparison is to disbelievers who despair that their dead will be raised and return alive.
rows.anchor: كما يئس الكفار من موتاهم أن يبعثوا ويرجعوا أحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min ashab al-qubur explains al-kuffar: people in graves recognized the ugliness of their state and evil destination and despaired of afterlife good.
rows.anchor: وقيل من اصحاب القبور بيان للكفار أي كما يئس الكفار الذين قبروا من خير الآخرة لأنهم تبينوا قبح حالهم وسوء منقلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven heavens طباقا are layers, one above another, like a shoe sole patched layer upon layer.
rows.anchor: مطابقة بعضها فوق بعض من طابق النعل إذا خصفها طبقا على طبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طباقا may be a verbal noun, mean possessing layers, or describe heavens as having been layered.
rows.anchor: وهذا وصف بالمصدر أو على ذات طباق أو على طوبقت طباقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another lexical analysis treats طباق as the plural of tabaq, like jamal and jimal.
rows.anchor: وقيل جمع طبق كجمل وجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in ما ترى may be to the Messenger or to any listener.
rows.anchor: الخطاب في ﴿ ما ترى في خلق الرحمن ﴾ للرسول أو لكل مخاطب

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Hamza and Ali read tafawut; it has the same meaning as tafawut, as taʿahud and taʿahud do.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من تفاوت ﴾ تفوت حمزة وعلى ومعنى البناءين واحد كالتعاهد والتعهد

rows.speaker: السدى
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses تفاوت as defect; the author's fuller definition is lack of proportion, when one part fails to fit another.
rows.anchor: وعن السدى من عيب وحقيقة التفاوت عدم التناسب كأن بعض الشيء يفوت بعضا ولا يلائمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause describes the layered heavens; their proportion demonstrates the Creator's overwhelming power to make such a harmonious creation.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة صفة لطباقا واصلها ما ترى فيهن من تفاوت وهو انه خلق الرحمن وانه بباهر قدرته هو الذي يخلق مثل ذلك الخلق المتناسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return the gaze to the sky and inspect it until observation confirms the report and leaves no doubt; futur means fissures or cracks, plural of fatr.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فارجع البصر ﴾ رده إلى السماء حتى يصح عندك ما اخبرت به بالمعاينة فلا تبقى معك شبهة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth gentle, easy, and fit to walk on without resistance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ هو الذي جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا ﴾ لينة سهلة مذللة لا تمنع المشي فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking on its shoulders is an instruction to seek provision or draw an inference; manakib may mean its mountains or its roads.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فامشوا في مناكبها ﴾ جوابها استدلالا استرزاقا أو جبالها أو طرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eat the provision God supplies on earth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكلوا من رزقه ﴾ أي من رزق الله فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will be raised to God, who will ask them how they thanked Him for His favors.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإليه النشور ﴾ أي وإليه نشوركم فهو سائلكم عن شكر ما أنعم به عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds above are birds in the air with their wings spread while flying, then drawing them in when they beat their sides.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولم يروا إلى الطير ﴾ جمع طائر ﴿ فوقهم ﴾ في الهواء ﴿ صافات ﴾ باسطات أجنحتهن في الجو عند طيرانهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The finite verb yaqbidna can be coordinated semantically with the participle, meaning they spread and contract, or with implied participles for both actions.
rows.anchor: ويقبضن معطوف على اسم الفاعل حملا على المعنى أي يصففن ويقبضن أو صافات وقابضات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wording treats spreading wings as the basic flight motion, like swimming through water, and wing strokes as an intermittent aid after the continuous spreading.
rows.anchor: واختيار هذا التركيب باعتبار أن اصل الطيران هو صف الأجنحة لأن الطيران في الهواء كالسباحة في الماء والهواء للطائر كالماء للسابح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Merciful alone keeps birds from falling during both spreading and contracting; by nature heavy things do not rise.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما يمسكهن ﴾ عن الوقوع عند القبض والبسط ﴿ إلا الرحمن ﴾ بقدرته وإلا فالثقيل طبعا حالا ولا يعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about what holds them may stand independently or be circumstantial from the pronoun in yaqbidna.
rows.anchor: وما يمسكهن مستأنف وان جعل حالا من الضمير في يقبضن يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees everything and knows how to create and govern these marvels.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنه بكل شيء بصير ﴾ يعلم كيف يخلق وكيف يدبر العجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One person walks face-down, falling and stumbling at every moment and wandering aimlessly; the other walks upright, safely, on a straight road.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه ﴾ أي ساقطا على وجهه يعثر كل ساعة ويمشي معتسفا وخير من ﴿ أهدى ﴾ أرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison asks which person is better guided; the straight path is an even road.
rows.anchor: ﴿ على صراط مستقيم ﴾ على طريق مستو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate after man is omitted because the word ahda already indicates it.
rows.anchor: وخبر من محذوف لدلالة اهدى عليه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the one face-down as Abu Jahl and the upright walker as the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي عني بالمكبأبو جهل وبالسوي النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means God will brand him by burning him on the nose as a mark of humiliation and identification.
rows.anchor: ﴿ سنسمه ﴾ سنكويه ﴿ على الخرطوم ﴾ على أنفه مهانة له وعلما يعرف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nose is singled out because branding there is especially ugly.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الأنف بالذكر لأن الوسم عليه أبشع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says he was struck on the nose with a sword at Badr, leaving a permanent mark.
rows.anchor: وقيل خطم بالسيف يوم بدر فبقيت سمة على خرطومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says al-Nadr ibn al-Harith demanded stones from heaven or painful punishment if the message were true.
rows.anchor: هو النضر بن الحرث قال ان كان هذا هو الحق من عندك فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء أو ائتنا بعذاب أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the Prophet prayed for punishment to descend on them.
rows.anchor: أو هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا بنزول العذاب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because saʾala is used with the meaning دعا, it governs bi, as in a caller who invokes punishment; دعا بكذا means to request it, as in 44:55.
rows.anchor: من قولك دعا بكذا إذا استدعاه وطلبه

rows.speaker: مدني وشامي
rows.claim: The Medinan and Syrian readings pronounce saʾala without hamza; it remains the verb for asking, with easing by softening, while sāʾil always has hamza by consensus.
rows.anchor: وسأل بغير همز مدني وشامي وهو من السؤال أيضا إلا انه خفف بالتليين وسائل مهموز اجماعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿruju means to ascend; a reading with yāʾ attaches the verb to the angels and Spirit.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تعرج ﴾ تصعد وبالياء على ﴿ الملائكة والروح ﴾

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel according to the majority, singled out after the general mention because of his excellence and honor.
rows.anchor: أي جبريل عليه السلام خصه بالذكر بعد العموم لفضله وشرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views identify the Spirit as an enormous angel, the greatest created after the Throne, or as believers' souls at death.
rows.anchor: أو خلق هم حفظة على الملائكة كما أن الملائكة حفظة علينا أو أرواح المؤمنين عند الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent is to God's Throne and the place where His command descends.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إليه ﴾ إلى عرشه ومهبط أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifty-thousand-year measure may attach to ascent and mean the time it would take an angel to rise by earthly years, or attach to the punishment's arrival and describe Judgment Day in human years.
rows.anchor: من سني الدنيا لو صعد فيه غبر الملك أو من صلة واقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The length may be figurative for how severe the day is for unbelievers, or its actual duration; one report describes fifty stations, each a thousand years.
rows.anchor: فأما ان يكون استطالة له لشدته على الكفار أو لأنه على الحقيقة كذلك فقد قيل فيه خمسون موطنا كل موطن ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That day feels to a believer no longer than the interval from noon to afternoon.
rows.anchor: وما قدر ذلك على المؤمن إلا كما بين الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be patient is linked to the question about punishment in 70:1: al-Nadr demanded it mockingly and denied revelation, which distressed the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاصبر ﴾ متعلق بسأل سائل لأن استعجال النضر بالعذاب إنما كان على وجه الاستهزاء برسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment is the day of requital and reckoning.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والذين يصدقون بيوم الدين ﴾ أي يوم الجزاء والحساب وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an is a lightened form of the emphatic anna, part of the revelation meaning that the matter is as follows.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأن ﴾ مخففة من الثقيلة يعني وأنه وهي من جملة الوحي أي أوحى إلى أن الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the unjust disbelievers had followed Islam's path, God would have given them abundant water.
rows.anchor: طريقة الاسلام ﴿ لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا ﴾ كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abundant water means expanded provision, since water is the cause of ample sustenance.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لوسعنا عليهم الرزق وذكر الماء الغدق لأنه سبب سعة الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not feed the poor as Muslims feed them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولم نك نطعم المسكين ﴾ كما يطعم المسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment is the reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكنا نكذب بيوم الدين ﴾ الحسب والجزاء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Amir and Asim read rabb al-samawati and rabb al-ardi in the genitive as apposition to rabbika.
rows.anchor: ﴿ رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما الرحمن ﴾ بجرهما ابن عامر وعاصم بدلا من ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative case, rabb may be the predicate of an omitted subject or a subject whose predicate is al-Rahman; al-Rahman may instead be its adjective, with la yamlikun as predicate.
rows.anchor: ومن رفعهما فرب خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو مبتدأ خبره الرحمن أو الرحمن صفته ولا يملكون خبرا وهما خبران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in la yamlikun refers to the inhabitants of the heavens and earth, and minhu refers to God.
rows.anchor: والضمير في لا يملكون لأهل السموات والأرض وفي منه خطابا لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khitaban may be the power to intercede against God's punishment, which belongs only by His leave, or the ability to address Him, which fear prevents.
rows.anchor: أي لا يملكون الشفاعة من عذابه تعالى إلا بإذنه أو لا يقدر أحد أن يخاطبه تعالى خوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If yawm is an adverb for la yamlikun, one should not pause at khitaban; if it modifies la yatakallamun, a pause there is allowed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يوم يقوم ﴾ إن جعلته ظرفا للايملكون لا تقف على خطابا وإن جعلته ظرفا للايتكلمون تقف

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel according to the majority.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الروح ﴾ جبريل عند الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the Spirit a mighty angel, the greatest creature God made after the Throne.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو ملك عظيم ما خلق الله تعالى بعد العرش خلقا أعظم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels stand in rows, with صفا functioning as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والملائكة صفا ﴾ حال أي مصطفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creatures do not speak from fear, except one whom the Merciful permits to speak or intercede.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا يتكلمون ﴾ أي الخلائق ثم خوفا ﴿ إلا من أذن له الرحمن ﴾ في الكلام أو الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking rightly may mean that an intercessor had said la ilaha illa Allah about the person in worldly life, or that only someone speaking correctly about intercession receives permission.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وقال صوابا ﴾ حقا بأن قال المشفوع له لا إله إلا الله في الدنيا أو لا يؤذن إلا لمن يتكلم بالصواب في أمر الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claimed that no lord stood above him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى ﴾ لا رب فوقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His people nevertheless had idols that they worshipped.
rows.anchor: وكانت لهم أصنام يعبدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day each person is occupied with his own concern, which is enough to keep him preoccupied and distract him from everyone else.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شأن ﴾ فى نفسه ﴿ يغنيه ﴾ يكفيه فى الاهتمام به ويشغله عن غيره
